ENHANCED_CASE_BASE.readiness_rationale: 73% of explanations are under 100 characters with no citations to any authoritative standard (ASC, COSO, IFRS, IAS, IMA). Only 20% of explanations are multi-sentence. 58 items at Apply/Analyze/Evaluate cognitive levels violate G-NEW-4 (one-sentence explanations). 37 numeric items with thin explanations represent the highest arithmetic risk. All 90 items lack per-item Difficulty/DifficultyScore metadata. This is the most critical uplift candidate — it needs explanation expansion, citation injection, numeric verification, and distractor rationale authoring before certification. However, its clean Unprocessed slate and consistent schema make it the best fit for a structured S509-S513 review pipeline.

universal_issues.description: Zero ExplanationWrong fields exist across all 400 case items in all 75 cases. The case-study format uses a single Explanation field per item for correct-answer reasoning only. No wrong-choice analysis, distractor rationale, or misconception identification is provided.
universal_issues.impact: Learners who select wrong answers receive no educational feedback on why their choice was wrong.
universal_issues.comparison_to_mcq: MCQ pack files use ExplanationWrongA-D fields (with known DL-008/026/021 defects) — but case files have the inverse problem: no distractor slots at all.
universal_issues.remediation: Either (a) extend the case schema to include ExplanationWrong fields per item, or (b) require the single Explanation field to address distractors inline.

universal_issues.description: All 400 case items across all 75 cases lack per-item Difficulty and DifficultyScore fields. Only case-level difficulty labels exist.
universal_issues.impact: Cannot calibrate per-item difficulty distribution; all items inherit the case-level label. DL-032 pattern (uniform Moderate labeling).

universal_issues.description: Across 400 case items, only 8 total citations to authoritative standards (ASC, COSO, IFRS, IAS, IMA). ENHANCED_CASE_BASE4 has the most (6). ENHANCED_CASE_BASE and ENHANCED_CASE_BASE5 have ZERO.
universal_issues.impact: Violates CAQS §4.1 (EV3 — explanations must reference governing accounting principle by name) and CAQS §14.2 (Gold Standard Checklist item: 'Explanation names governing standard').

universal_issues.description: Exhibit ReferencedBy arrays are empty for 42 of 75 cases (56%). This degrades from ENHANCED_CASE_BASE (0/15 with refs) to ENHANCED_CASE_BASE5 (8/15 with refs), showing progressive improvement across packs.
universal_issues.impact: Schema completeness issue — cannot validate that all exhibits are consumed by items (CAQS §3.4 rule 3: 'No decorative data').

universal_issues.description: 37 of 54 Certified cases (68.5%) across Base2-Base5 have question_state: 'Certified' but ProductionStatus: 'Draft'. Only 3 Certified cases have ProductionStatus: 'Production'.
universal_issues.impact: State inconsistency — the governance framework has two competing state fields. 'Certified' + 'Draft' is a contradictory combination.

universal_issues.description: The first case in each array (CBQ-A1, CBQ2-A3, CBQ3-A1, CBQ4-A1, CBQ5-B2) is Unprocessed while nearly all other cases are Certified. These first cases typically lack CompanyName and Stakeholder metadata.
universal_issues.impact: Likely a pipeline artifact — the first case was authored as a template header and never completed.

certification_quality_concern.summary: 54 of 75 cases (72%) across Base2-Base5 are marked Certified, but the certification basis is opaque. Certified items have: zero ExplanationWrong fields, 0-5 standard citations per array, missing per-item Difficulty/DifficultyScore, inconsistent ProductionStatus, and DL-023 exhibit issues. This does not meet CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification requirements.
certification_quality_concern.recommendation: Re-verify all 54 Certified cases under CAQS §1.6 before relying on their certification status for learner delivery.

s509_s513_pattern_fit.analysis: The S509-S513 'uplift/review/certify' pattern involves explanation enhancement, citation injection, distractor rationale authoring, numeric verification, and metadata completion — followed by CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification and certification.
s509_s513_pattern_fit.best_fit_rationale: ENHANCED_CASE_BASE (scored_cases.js, 15 cases, 90 items) is the strongest fit because: (1) It has the largest quality gap — 73% thin explanations, 0 citations, 0 Certifications, making the uplift impact highest. (2) All 15 cases are cleanly Unprocessed — no re-verification of questionable prior certifications needed. (3) It has 37 numeric items (highest) requiring systematic arithmetic audit. (4) The schema is stable (parseable, no missing case fields, 0 exhibit issues). (5) All cases share the same structural template (consistent schema), enabling batch processing. The S509-S513 pipeline applied to this array would transform the weakest case bank into a certified one with the highest marginal improvement.
s509_s513_pattern_fit.secondary_rationale: ENHANCED_CASE_BASE4 is the best secondary target because: (1) It has 3 Unprocessed cases needing full uplift. (2) It has the best existing citation coverage (6 citations) — expanding these is lower effort. (3) The 12 Certified cases need re-verification (lower priority) but the 3 Unprocessed ones could be uplifted alongside Base's cases. (4) 5 DL-023 exhibit issues need repair.
s509_s513_pattern_fit.deferred_scheduling: ENHANCED_CASE_BASE2, ENHANCED_CASE_BASE3, ENHANCED_CASE_BASE5 — these arrays are already 80-93% Certified. Uplift should focus on re-verifying the existing certification against CAQS §1.6 (adding citations, per-item Difficulty, ReferencedBy) rather than a full greenfield uplift. Their Unprocessed cases (1 each) need targeted uplift and can be fast-followed after Base.

2. ENHANCED_CASE_BASE4 — Unprocessed cases uplift (3 cases) + Certified re-verification (12 cases)
3. ENHANCED_CASE_BASE2 — Unprocessed case uplift (1 case) + Certified re-verification (14 cases)
4. ENHANCED_CASE_BASE3 — Unprocessed case uplift (1 case) + Certified re-verification (14 cases)
